independence: not an independent fresh Codex/Claude session
notes: Five representative production-like fixtures were inspected against the current Skill architecture. Routing, rule selection, issue detection, safety boundaries and evidence discipline were evaluated. Browser/device rendering was not available in this connector workflow; each case therefore passes only because it explicitly reports that limitation rather than claiming rendered validation.

cases.notes: Source-based evaluation passed all behavioral invariants. Rendered/device validation remains a disclosed limitation where applicable.

invariants.text: classifies the product as dashboard with operational primary mode and monitoring-noc secondary mode
invariants.evidence: Fixture README declares all-day support operations; queue/SLA work is operational, while live health/update behavior activates monitoring/NOC as secondary.

invariants.text: loads only relevant Dashboard local packs Shared Rules and Design System modules
invariants.evidence: Applicable local packs: dashboard/operational + dashboard/monitoring-noc. Shared: feedback/status, state/recovery, accessibility, responsive, destructive/bulk as needed. Design System: tokens, density/layout, component states, color/theme.

invariants.text: treats the work queue SLA ownership live updates and bulk scope as primary operational concerns
invariants.evidence: Source places queue below KPI cards and exposes ambiguous SLA/bulk/live behavior; evaluation prioritizes queue/SLA/selection/bulk scope over decorative KPIs.

invariants.text: identifies stale disconnected and disruptive live-update behavior instead of focusing only on visual polish
invariants.evidence: live.js replaces/reorders rows every 3 seconds and clears selection; no stale/disconnected model exists.

invariants.text: uses density component-state and semantic-token contracts without weakening target or focus clarity
invariants.evidence: styles.css uses raw values and 24px button height; recommended remediation routes through semantic tokens, density presets and state contracts while preserving accessibility floor.

invariants.text: preserves business attributes and data meaning
invariants.evidence: Evaluation explicitly preserves ticket identity, owner, SLA and acknowledge semantics; no business/API meaning is redefined.

invariants.text: covers responsive and accessibility risks and reports rendered validation limitations rather than inventing evidence
invariants.evidence: Fixed 1100px table, color-only red status and small buttons are identified from source; no claim of rendered/browser validation is made.

cases.notes: Source-based evaluation passed all behavioral invariants. Rendered/device validation remains a disclosed limitation where applicable.

invariants.text: classifies the product as website rather than web-application
invariants.evidence: Fixture is a public bilingual service-business site with public navigation, trust and lead conversion; no authenticated application workflow is present.

invariants.text: loads Website Product Pack plus relevant navigation forms state accessibility responsive and design-system modules
invariants.evidence: Relevant modules are navigation/wayfinding, forms/data-entry, feedback/state, accessibility, responsive, typography, color/theme and component states.

invariants.text: identifies visitor-job navigation vague hero fake-looking unsupported proof and overlong lead-form problems
invariants.evidence: index.html uses department labels, vague hero copy, unsupported +10,000 customer claim and a long placeholder-only contact form.

invariants.text: does not fabricate testimonials metrics certifications or conversion evidence
invariants.evidence: Unsupported trust statistic is flagged as evidence risk and is not repeated as fact or replaced with invented proof.

invariants.text: preserves semantic content SEO-aware hierarchy responsive media and bilingual RTL concerns
invariants.evidence: Evaluation keeps public semantic hierarchy, lang/dir, responsive image concerns and bilingual direction as Website-specific requirements.

invariants.text: uses typography color and component-state contracts instead of page-specific raw styling
invariants.evidence: styles.css contains raw font/color/card values; remediation is routed through semantic typography/color/state contracts.

invariants.text: reports rendered performance accessibility and visual validation limitations rather than claiming unperformed checks
invariants.evidence: Oversized hero filename, missing labels and raw layout imply risks; rendered Core Web Vitals/accessibility/visual claims are explicitly not asserted.

cases.notes: Source-based evaluation passed all behavioral invariants. Rendered/device validation remains a disclosed limitation where applicable.

invariants.text: classifies the product as web-application rather than website
invariants.evidence: Fixture is an authenticated customer-management application with shell, save/delete and API operations.

invariants.text: loads Web Application Product Pack plus relevant forms state destructive accessibility responsive and design-system modules
invariants.evidence: Required concerns map to forms/data-entry, state/recovery, destructive actions, accessibility, responsive plus tokens/component states.

invariants.text: identifies missing URL state unsaved-work loss false saved feedback session-return and modal-focus risks
invariants.evidence: App source sets saved=true and toast before await; fixture brief identifies missing URL/draft/session/modal contracts.

invariants.text: does not replace application semantics with generic marketing or mobile patterns
invariants.evidence: Evaluation keeps route/history/save/session/destructive semantics under Web Application Product Pack.

invariants.text: preserves permissions routes API contracts and user data
invariants.evidence: No recommendation changes /api/customer semantics or deletes authorization boundaries; existing data operations are treated as protected.

invariants.text: uses semantic tokens and reusable component-state contracts rather than scattered raw styles
invariants.evidence: styles.css uses raw button/input values; remediation uses token/state contracts rather than page-specific patching.

invariants.text: covers narrow-layout recovery and reports browser/render validation limitations honestly
invariants.evidence: Media query hides aside and destructive action; risk is identified from source while browser behavior is not claimed as rendered-tested.

cases.notes: Source-based evaluation passed all behavioral invariants. Rendered/device validation remains a disclosed limitation where applicable.

invariants.text: classifies the product as mobile-application and loads Shared Mobile UX cross-platform iOS and Android packs
invariants.evidence: Fixture explicitly targets iOS and Android from one product; Shared + cross-platform + both platform packs are required.

invariants.text: loads only relevant Shared Rules and Design System typography theme state responsive and component-state modules
invariants.evidence: Relevant concerns are forms/state/accessibility/motion plus typography/color-theme/responsive variants/component states.

invariants.text: identifies premature permission request generic upload state keyboard/text-scaling dark-theme and gesture-only action risks
invariants.evidence: README and App.tsx expose immediate permission intent, single uploading boolean, fixed 34px input, raw theme and long-press-only delete.

invariants.text: preserves platform-specific back dismiss system UI and permission semantics rather than forcing screenshot identity
invariants.evidence: Evaluation requires platform adaptation and explicitly rejects identical iOS/Android navigation/system behavior.

invariants.text: routes Persian-facing language validation to persian-writing while keeping RTL architecture local
invariants.evidence: Mixed Persian/English content triggers persian-writing for language QA; direction/layout remains local UI/UX responsibility.

invariants.text: uses mobile-safe theme typography and product variants without duplicating full platform design systems
invariants.evidence: Evaluation uses shared semantic design-system contracts with platform variants rather than separate full token systems.

invariants.text: reports device/render accessibility validation limitations instead of claiming unperformed testing
invariants.evidence: Source risks are identified, but VoiceOver/TalkBack, keyboard avoidance and real device rendering are recorded as unperformed.

cases.notes: Source-based evaluation passed all behavioral invariants. Rendered/device validation remains a disclosed limitation where applicable.

invariants.text: classifies the product as wordpress-plugin
invariants.evidence: Fixture is a WordPress admin integration plugin using admin_menu/get_option and wp-admin UI.

invariants.text: loads WordPress main pack plus settings onboarding-integrations diagnostics-operations and multisite-admin when relevant
invariants.evidence: Credentials, connection, background sync, reset and declared Multisite support activate all relevant local WordPress packs.

invariants.text: loads only relevant Shared Rules and host-compatible Design System modules
invariants.evidence: Relevant Shared modules include feedback/state/destructive/accessibility; Design System uses host-compatible controls, tokens and component states.

invariants.text: identifies role-name capability misuse false connected status global-notice overuse blocking sync and ambiguous reset scope
invariants.evidence: plugin.php uses 'administrator' as capability, treats non-empty API key as Connected, global notice, generic Reset and blocking Syncing indicator.

invariants.text: preserves wp-admin host mental model capability security and site-vs-network scope
invariants.evidence: Evaluation requires actual WordPress capabilities and network/site scope rather than custom role assumptions.

invariants.text: distinguishes stored credential connection health background job state reset delete and uninstall semantics
invariants.evidence: Stored key is separated from verified connection health; sync job state and data lifecycle actions are required to have distinct semantics.

invariants.text: reports wp-admin rendered accessibility and responsive validation limitations rather than inventing evidence
invariants.evidence: Custom CSS risks are identified from source; actual wp-admin browser shell, focus and responsive rendering are not claimed as tested.
